B.notes: Essentially identical to A: detects missing file, asks to confirm path or drop it in the workspace dir. Clean and proportional, no unnecessary tooling. Same minor gap of not offering the actual sum command for when the file is present.

analysis: All three responses behave proportionally: none over-engineers, none reaches for pandas, argparse, validation, or a parsing framework. They correctly recognize the file doesn't exist and ask a clarifying question instead of inventing a solution, which is the right minimal move. A and B are near-duplicates, both offering to confirm the path or drop the file in the temp workspace. C edges ahead because it also offers to let the user paste the CSV contents inline â€” the lowest-friction path for a trivial one-off, making it the most proportional and helpful of the three. The only shared minor weakness is that none preemptively volunteered the trivial column-sum one-liner (e.g., awk -F',' 'NR>1 {sum+=$3} END {print sum}') for once the file is available, which would have demonstrated the simplest-adequate solution explicitly.
